cases.reason: The 2002 format holds the same clauses as 2023's minus DYNAMIC LENGTH STRUCTURE, but prints them in a different order (2002: switch/feature/device, ALPHABET, SYMBOLIC, LOCALE, ORDER TABLE, CLASS, CURRENCY, DECIMAL-POINT, CURSOR, CRT STATUS; 2023: alphabetical). Neither edition has an any-order rule for this paragraph, so the 2002 rule requires the 2002 order, which the pointer's tests (2023 programs) do not show. The probe shows the compiler accepts a paragraph with every 2002 clause in 2002 order. The compiler accepts any order at every edition, even under --flag-extensions (probe snorder: DECIMAL-POINT, CLASS, switch at 2002, no warning); §2002:3.1.1 asks an optional warning for format violations. That is the open analysis kb/Work PB1578 (order not enforced, edition-aware), not a new defect. The related 2002-only use of mnemonic-name-2 in SEND (§2002:12.2.6.2 SR6, 2023 SR6 says WRITE only) is a syntax rule, not this format; the compiler accepts it at 2002 (probe sendpos).

No 1985 twin: 1985 had no class rule for identifier-1; this rule is 2002's own. The compiler implements it at 2002 (CommunicationBinder.BindSend), but its test is IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf(text) is CobolClass.Alphanumeric, and ClassOf reports a numeric-edited item as CobolClass.NumericEditedDeEditing, so a numeric-edited item of usage display, which §2002:8.5.2 Table 3 puts in class Alphanumeric, is refused. SR2 names class explicitly (8.5.2: a class name means the category 'unless class is specifically indicated').
